In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the results of the present study do not support the use of posttreatment blood as a surrogate measure of pretreatment levels of DDT and its metabolites, but do support its use in studies examining PCBs.

the use of posttreatment blood for the purpose of measuring organochlorines in breast cancer cases may be appropriate, but only after a thorough evaluation of the effects of treatment on blood levels of the specific chemicals under study.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of posttreatment blood for characterizing organochlorines is not appropriate for breast cancer studies.
the use of pretreatment blood samples for breast cancer case-control studies is preferable to the use of posttreatment samples.
blood samples collected after the commencement of treatment for breast cancer may be used to characterize DDE levels, but may underestimate PCB levels.
The main takeaway from our work is that
posttreatment samples may be used to estimate pretreatment levels of DDT, but may not accurately estimate pretreatment levels for PCBs.
blood samples drawn after treatment for breast cancers are not suitable for use as a proxy for pretreatment samples in studies that examine organochlorine exposure and breast cancer risk.
the timing of blood collection relative to treatment is important when assessing breast cancer risk associated with exposure to DDE or PCB.
